title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
problem: Context-free grammar (CFG) constrained decoding for LLMs is slow because every token generation step requires recomputing token masks from scratch, dominating inference latency for structured output generation.
motivation: Applications requiring JSON, SQL, or other structured outputs from LLMs depend on constrained decoding, but existing systems (Outlines, llama.cpp grammar) add 10-100x overhead per token. Eliminating redundant computation would make structured generation practical for high-throughput serving.
method: XGrammar splits the token vocabulary into context-independent tokens (whose acceptance can be precomputed offline once per grammar) and context-dependent tokens (requiring runtime evaluation). For Llama-3.1 with JSON grammar, only 1,134 of 128k tokens are context-dependent (<1%). A persistent pushdown automaton stack tracks parser state. Context expansion reduces context-dependent tokens further (to ~120, a 90% reduction). An adaptive token mask cache stores masks per parser state, with 0.2% memory overhead. CPU-GPU overlap hides remaining mask computation behind GPU attention.
key_novelty: Context-independent/context-dependent token split that precomputes >99% of token masks offline, combined with a persistent pushdown automaton and adaptive token mask cache, achieving near-zero constrained decoding overhead.
contributions: Context-independent vs context-dependent token classification for pushdown automata
Offline precomputation of context-independent token masks (>99% of vocabulary)
Context expansion algorithm reducing context-dependent tokens by 90%
Persistent execution stack for efficient parser state management
Adaptive token mask cache with 0.2% memory overhead (160MB to 0.46MB)
CPU-GPU overlap hiding remaining runtime mask computation
Up to 100x per-token speedup; 80x end-to-end serving vs vLLM+Outlines

metrics.speedup: Up to 100x per-token speedup; 80x end-to-end serving throughput vs vLLM+Outlines
metrics.accuracy: Exact grammar compliance; no accuracy loss vs unconstrained sampling within grammar
metrics.other: Context-dependent tokens: <1% of vocabulary (1134/128k for Llama-3.1); mask cache 0.46MB vs 160MB naive

limitations: Context expansion has worst-case exponential complexity for certain grammar structures
Cache effectiveness depends on grammar and input distribution
Context-dependent token computation still required at runtime for complex grammars
Primarily evaluated on JSON grammar; other grammar types may have higher context-dependent ratios
